purpose: Current, provenance-rich hypothesis routing. Entries are not proof and contain no spray payloads.

techniques.title: Successful errors for blind code injection and SSTI
techniques.safe_validation: Compare inert expression, invalid syntax, and harmless deterministic output or timing controls; stop before unsafe execution.

techniques.title: ORM relationship and filter data leakage
techniques.safe_validation: Use synthetic records and owned tenants to compare result counts, ordering, errors, and field visibility across relation paths.

techniques.title: Blind SSRF visibility through redirect-loop behavior
techniques.safe_validation: Use a researcher-controlled callback and benign redirect chain; do not target internal metadata or third-party systems.

techniques.title: Unicode normalization differentials
techniques.safe_validation: Compare canonically equivalent owned identifiers through each parser and guard; record normalization points without bypassing unrelated controls.

techniques.title: SOAP proxy and WSDL trust-boundary analysis
techniques.safe_validation: Trace WSDL-controlled configuration into generated clients in a local harness; use a harmless marker rather than production code execution.

techniques.title: Cross-site ETag length side channel
techniques.safe_validation: Use two controlled account states and synthetic content; measure only the minimum distinction needed to establish an oracle.

techniques.title: Framework internal cache poisoning chains
techniques.safe_validation: Use unique canaries and a disposable cache key; compare cache miss/hit controls and avoid poisoning shared user traffic.

techniques.title: Cross-origin redirect connection-pool side channel
techniques.safe_validation: Use controlled redirect destinations and owned states, repeat with browser isolation, and distinguish timing noise from a real oracle.

techniques.title: HTTP/2 CONNECT interpretation and routing boundaries
techniques.safe_validation: Validate only against an owned listener or approved lab endpoint; do not scan internal address ranges.

techniques.title: Parser differential vulnerability research
techniques.safe_validation: Build a local differential corpus and identify one input interpreted differently across adjacent components before testing a minimal benign case.

techniques.title: Broken access control
techniques.safe_validation: Use researcher-owned principals, objects, and tenants to build an intended-versus-observed authorization matrix.

techniques.title: Security misconfiguration
techniques.safe_validation: Confirm the exact reachable configuration and sensitive effect; avoid broad service scanning or third-party data access.

techniques.title: Software supply chain failures
techniques.safe_validation: Trace provenance, version resolution, signatures, and build inputs in a local or owned pipeline; do not publish malicious packages.

techniques.title: Injection
techniques.safe_validation: Use harmless deterministic markers, invalid-input controls, and a local harness where impact could be destructive.

techniques.title: Authentication failures
techniques.safe_validation: Use only researcher-controlled accounts and tokens; compare fresh, expired, revoked, wrong-audience, and wrong-role controls.

techniques.title: Software or data integrity failures
techniques.safe_validation: Use a controlled unsigned or altered artifact in a disposable environment and verify the intended trust check.

techniques.title: Mishandling of exceptional conditions
techniques.safe_validation: Trigger bounded invalid or interrupted states with synthetic data and verify rollback, authorization, and fail-closed behavior.

techniques.title: Broken object level authorization
techniques.safe_validation: Swap only owned object identifiers between controlled principals and compare with intended public-sharing behavior.

techniques.title: Broken authentication
techniques.safe_validation: Use supplied test credentials and controlled lifecycle states; never use stolen credentials or credential stuffing.

techniques.title: Broken object property level authorization
techniques.safe_validation: Compare visible, writable, and returned properties across controlled roles with synthetic values.

techniques.title: Unrestricted resource consumption
techniques.safe_validation: Use analytical limits, a local harness, or a tiny bounded request set; do not stress production.

techniques.title: Unrestricted access to sensitive business flows
techniques.safe_validation: Model the invariant and use one or two reversible synthetic transactions; do not create spam, scarcity, or financial harm.

techniques.title: Server-side request forgery
techniques.safe_validation: Use a researcher-owned callback and localhost in a lab; do not access cloud metadata or internal third-party services.

techniques.title: Improper inventory management
techniques.safe_validation: Correlate documented and observed versions, then make one benign request to an explicitly in-scope endpoint.

techniques.title: Unsafe consumption of APIs
techniques.safe_validation: Replace the integration with an owned stub and verify validation, transport, authorization, redirects, and error handling.

techniques.title: Agentic application trust and control failures
techniques.safe_validation: Use synthetic tools, canary secrets, owned data, explicit approval controls, and a local sandbox; never let untrusted content expand authority.

techniques.title: Hidden state-machine and partial-construction race conditions
techniques.safe_validation: Model one owned-data invariant, run stable sequential baselines, use bounded protocol-correct synchronization, wait for asynchronous settlement, and compare authoritative final state.

techniques.title: HTTP/2 single-packet and HTTP/1.1 last-byte race delivery
techniques.safe_validation: Fingerprint the negotiated protocol, begin with two owned-data lanes, preserve delivery limitations, and stop at the smallest repeatable authoritative-state violation.

techniques.title: Improper synchronization of security-sensitive shared state
techniques.safe_validation: Use an owned local regression with a deterministic barrier or scheduler, fixed seed, clean datastore, authoritative state assertion, and patched synchronization differential.

techniques.title: Time-of-check time-of-use security decision gap
techniques.safe_validation: Insert a deterministic local barrier between the check and use, alter only researcher-owned state, verify the crossed invariant, and confirm the atomic or revalidated fix.

techniques.title: Objective-led hacker-powered penetration-test coverage
techniques.safe_validation: Translate engagement objectives into a coverage plan, record completed and deferred lanes, and preserve evidence quality gates for every candidate.
